examDifficulty.heading: Is the Public Sector Solutions Accredited Professional Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam. Public Sector Solutions has ready-made processes for licences, permits, inspections, grants and benefits, each with its own records. Most questions ask which of these fits an agency's need.
bullets: About 65% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers. Check the official guide for the current figure.
Process areas. Licensing and permitting, inspections, grants, benefits and case management.
Tools. OmniStudio for forms and guided steps, and Experience Cloud for constituent portals.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Walk through one licence application from submission to approval and inspection in a trial org before the exam. Before you book. Aim for 75% or more on practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Public Sector Solutions Accredited Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are taken online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe an agency task, such as issuing a food business licence or paying out a grant, and ask which feature or record handles it.
bestWayToPass: Learn each process area: What records licensing, inspections, grants and benefits use, and how they connect.
Follow an application: From the public form, through review and approval, to the issued licence or award.
Know OmniStudio's role: Intake forms, guided steps and data lookups are often built with it.
Think about the constituent: Self-service portals, status updates and accessible forms.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests how you set up Public Sector Solutions: licensing and permitting, inspections, grants, benefits, case management and constituent self-service.

keyConcepts.h2: Public Sector Solutions AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Case Management for Government
blocks.body: Agencies handle many kinds of cases, such as complaints, investigations and service requests. Public Sector Solutions builds on Service Cloud case management and adds features for government work, such as **interviews**, **investigations** and tracking the people and organisations involved. Cases can be routed to the right team, linked to related records like licences or inspections, and tracked against deadlines. Sensitive cases need tight sharing so only the right staff can see them.

blocks.heading: Licensing & Permitting
blocks.body: Businesses and people apply for **licences** and **permits**, such as a food business licence or a building permit. A **regulatory authorization type** defines each kind of licence and its rules. An **application** is submitted, often through a public portal form, then reviewed, with checks, fees and approvals. When approved, the licence is issued as a record with an expiry date, and renewals can be handled the same way. Applicants can see the status of their application online.

blocks.heading: Grants Management
blocks.body: Agencies that give out money use **grants management**. A **funding opportunity** describes what is on offer and who can apply. Organisations submit **applications**, which are reviewed and scored by reviewers. Approved applications become **awards**, with a budget and conditions. Money is paid out in **disbursements**, often tied to milestones or reports from the grantee. This keeps a full record of how public money was given and used.

blocks.heading: Inspections & Compliance
blocks.body: Inspectors visit sites to check rules are being followed, for example a restaurant's hygiene or a building's safety. Inspections are planned as **visits**, with **assessment tasks** and indicators that the inspector completes, often on a mobile device in the field. Results can be pass, fail or need follow-up. Failed checks can lead to **violations** and enforcement actions, and repeat inspections can be scheduled. Results link back to the business and its licence.

blocks.heading: Constituent Engagement & Digital Experience
blocks.body: Members of the public expect to apply, pay and check status online. **Experience Cloud** portals let constituents submit applications, upload documents and track progress. **OmniStudio** tools often power the forms: **OmniScripts** guide people step by step, and **Integration Procedures** and **Data Mappers** fetch and save data. Forms should be accessible and work on phones. Many agencies run on **Government Cloud**, which meets public sector security standards.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Public Sector Solutions Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions name an agency process. Match it to the right area (licensing, inspections, grants, benefits or cases), then the record that represents it.

blocks.heading: Public Sector Data Model
blocks.body: Each process area has its own records: authorization types and applications for licences, funding opportunities and awards for grants, visits and assessments for inspections.

blocks.heading: Grants Management
blocks.body: Funding opportunity, application, review, award, then disbursements. Payments can depend on milestones.

blocks.heading: Licensing & Permitting
blocks.body: Define licence types with regulatory authorization types. Applications move through review to an issued licence with an expiry date.

blocks.heading: Constituent 360 & Self-Service
blocks.body: Portals let constituents apply, pay and track status. Staff see the full history in one place.

blocks.heading: OmniStudio for Government
blocks.body: OmniScripts for guided public forms. Integration Procedures for fetching data from other systems.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Public Sector Solutions:

sampleQuestions.question: A city wants businesses to apply for a food business licence online and track their application. What should be set up?
options: A licence application process with a public portal form
sampleQuestions.explanation: Licensing and permitting handles applications, review and issuing licences, and a portal lets applicants apply and track status.
whyWrong: Grants are for giving out money, not issuing licences.

sampleQuestions.question: Where are the rules and settings for each kind of licence, such as a liquor licence, defined?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Regulatory authorization types describe each licence or permit type and its rules.

sampleQuestions.question: An inspector visits a restaurant and must complete a hygiene checklist on a tablet. What should be used?
options: An inspection visit with assessment tasks
sampleQuestions.explanation: Inspections are planned as visits, with assessment tasks the inspector completes in the field.

sampleQuestions.question: A restaurant fails its hygiene inspection. What should happen next in the system?
options: Record a violation and schedule a follow-up inspection
sampleQuestions.explanation: Failed checks can lead to violations and repeat inspections, linked to the business and its licence.
whyWrong: Closing the account removes the history.
Failing doesn't earn a new licence.

sampleQuestions.question: A state agency offers $2 million in community grants. Where should the details of what is on offer and who can apply be recorded?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Funding opportunities describe the grant, its rules and who can apply.
whyWrong: Benefit enrollments are for individuals receiving benefits.

sampleQuestions.question: A grant has been awarded. Money should be paid in three parts as the grantee reaches milestones. What should be used?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Disbursements record payments, and can be linked to milestones or reports.
whyWrong: One upfront payment removes control over progress.

sampleQuestions.question: Grant applications must be scored by a panel of reviewers before decisions are made. What fits?
options: Application review with assigned reviewers and scoring
sampleQuestions.explanation: Grants management supports reviews where reviewers score applications.
whyWrong: Dashboards show results, they don't run reviews.
An inbox isn't a structured review.

sampleQuestions.question: The public intake form has many steps and needs to look up data from another government system. Which tools fit?
options: An OmniScript with an Integration Procedure
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScripts guide people through steps, and Integration Procedures fetch data from other systems.
whyWrong: A text field can't guide or look up data.

sampleQuestions.question: An investigation into a complaint involves interviews with several people. Which area handles this?
options: Case management with investigations and interviews
sampleQuestions.explanation: Public sector case management includes features for investigations and interviews.

sampleQuestions.question: A licence expires each year. How should renewals be handled?
options: By changing the expiry date by hand each year
By deleting and recreating the licence
Through a renewal application linked to the existing licence
sampleQuestions.explanation: Renewals can follow the same application process, linked to the existing licence for a clear history.
whyWrong: Phone-only is slow and hard to track.
Manual date changes skip checks and fees.

sampleQuestions.question: An agency needs its Salesforce org to meet public sector security standards. What should it consider?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Government Cloud is designed to meet public sector security and compliance standards.

sampleQuestions.question: A complaint is linked to a business that holds a licence and had a failed inspection. Why link these records?
options: So staff can see the full history of the business in one place
sampleQuestions.explanation: Linked records give staff a full view of the business, which helps with decisions.
whyWrong: Fees are set by licence rules.

sampleQuestions.question: Constituents should be able to upload documents and see their application status on their phone. What matters most?
options: An accessible, mobile-friendly Experience Cloud portal
sampleQuestions.explanation: Portals should work on phones and be accessible to everyone.
whyWrong: Hiding status leads to more calls.

sampleQuestions.question: Sensitive investigation cases should only be visible to the investigations team. What should be used?
options: Private sharing settings with access granted to that team
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tight sharing keeps sensitive cases visible only to the right staff.
whyWrong: Chatter groups don't control case access.
Public Read Only shows them to everyone.

sampleQuestions.question: Which records make up the main grants flow?
options: Funding opportunity, application, award and disbursements
sampleQuestions.explanation: Grants move from the opportunity on offer, to applications, to awards, to payments.
